   391	\begin{lemma}[Extraction of the EPR state and the Pauli observables]\label{lem:qld-unitary}
   392		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ExtractionWitness}
   393		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaExtract}
   394		\uses{lem:qld-4-7, def:v-swap-unitary, def:expanded-state, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
   395		There is a universal constant $C_{\mathrm{ext}}\geq1$. Set
   396		\[
   397			\delta_P^{\mathrm{ext}}=C_{\mathrm{ext}}B,
   398			\qquad
   399			\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}=C_{\mathrm{ext}}
   400			\left((\delta_P^{\mathrm{ext}})^{1/4}+\frac{md}{q}\right).
   401		\]
   402		There exist unitaries $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $V_{\mathrm{B}}$ acting on registers $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, such that the following hold.
   403		\begin{enumerate}
   404			\item There exists a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ such that
   405			\[
   406				\bigl\| V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}}_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \bigr\|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   407			\]
   408			\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
   409			\begin{align*}
   410				V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \bigl(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \bigr)_{\mathrm{A}} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''}\;, \\
   411				V_{\mathrm{B}} \, \bigl(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \bigr)_{\mathrm{B}} \, V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   412			\end{align*}
   413			where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''}$, with the answer summation over $h \in \F_q^{M}$ and no average over questions.
   414		\end{enumerate}
   415		The unitaries may be taken to be $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{B}}$ of Definition~\ref{def:v-swap-unitary}.
   416		The conditional result below assumes the global polynomial-pair measurement
   417		of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, whereas the present proof obtains that measurement
   418		from the lemma. It therefore establishes the extraction conclusions only
   419		after the measurement and its consistency estimates are supplied, not the
   420		existence claim above. The missing composition and the range-projection
   421		transfer are recorded in \cite{gap:qpbt_extraction-transfer}.
   422	\end{lemma}
   423	\begin{proof}
   424		\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, lem:v-swap-conjugation, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:qld-construct-the-paulis, lem:qld-win-implications, fact:triangle-for-simeq, def:bracket, lem:cancellation, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree, lem:qld-4-7}
   425		For the first item, the self-consistency of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ (Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}) is equivalent, since these observables are Hermitian involutions (Lemma~\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}), to $\E_{j \in \{0,\ldots,t-1\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M} \bra{\hat\psi} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ot \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat\psi} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$; setting $\ket{\vartheta} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$ and using the exact conjugation identities of Lemma~\ref{lem:v-swap-conjugation}, this becomes $\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$, where $H_W = \E_j \E_{\tilde{u}} \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \bigl( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \ot \tau^W(s) \bigr)^{\ot M}$ by the tensor factorization of $\tau^W(\tilde{u})$ and the invariance of the uniform average over $s$ under $s \mapsto e_j s$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:cancellation}, $\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \ot \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ on each pair of qudits, whence $H_X H_Z = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$. The bounds $\| (\Id - H_W)\ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq \delta_P$ and $\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_P$, combined through the triangle inequality $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ (see Remark~\ref{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}), give $\bra{\vartheta} \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 4\delta_P$.
   426		% Case distinction added: the source normalizes the projected vector
   427		% without ensuring that it is nonzero; see Remark rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip.
   428		If $\delta_P > 1/8$, then, after enlarging the universal constant in $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, both items of the lemma hold with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ an arbitrary unit state, since their left-hand sides never exceed $4$; assume therefore $\delta_P \leq 1/8$. Then the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ has squared norm at least $1 - 4\delta_P \geq 1/2 > 0$, and $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ may be defined as its normalization; the overlap of $\ket{\vartheta}$ with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ equals the norm of that vector and is at least $\sqrt{1 - 4\delta_P} \geq 1 - 4\delta_P$, which yields the first item with a bound of $8\delta_P = O(\sqrt{\delta_P})$. For the second item, Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} gives, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$, $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ and $\Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \simeq_\eps M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \Id$, where $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h$; combining these with Item~1 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} by Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle-for-simeq}, using $\eps \leq \sqrt{\eps} \leq \delta_P$, yields $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}} \Id \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$.    397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.

   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree).

   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. 1	# Formalization Patterns
     2	
     3	Key design patterns used in the MIPStarRE Lean formalization to bridge the
     4	gap between paper-level mathematics and a compilable Lean proof.
     5	
     6	This document is intended for contributors who need to understand *why* the
     7	Lean code is structured as it is, and for reviewers who need to recognize
     8	these patterns when reading PRs.  It complements the individual chapter audits
     9	in `audits/`, the proof-integrity rules in the lean-conventions skill (addenda:
    10	`docs/project_conventions.md`), and the
    11	proof-gap protocol in `docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.
    12	
    13	## Table of Contents
    14	
    15	1. [Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations](#pattern-1-source-faithful-statements-and-internal-proof-obligations)
    16	2. [Blueprint–Lean synchronization](#pattern-2-blueprintlean-synchronization)
    17	3. [Split-module architecture](#pattern-3-split-module-architecture)
    18	4. [Public re-export pattern](#pattern-4-public-re-export-pattern)
    19	5. [Temporary obligation-structure pattern](#pattern-5-temporary-obligation-structure-pattern)
    20	6. [Paper-gap documentation pattern](#pattern-6-paper-gap-documentation-pattern)
    21	
    22	---
    23	
    24	## Pattern 1: Source-faithful statements and internal proof obligations
    25	
    26	### The rule
    27	
    28	A declaration presented as the formalization of a paper theorem, lemma,
    29	proposition, or corollary must state the paper result, up to faithful formal
    30	encoding of the mathematical domain.  Its public hypotheses and conclusion are
    31	both part of the statement.  Adding a load-bearing bridge, residual, repair,
    32	obligation-structure input, hypotheses bundle, or assumptions bundle not present
    33	in the cited statement changes the theorem into a conditional helper.
    34	
    35	The project therefore distinguishes three objects.
    36	
    37	| Object | Public statement | Blueprint status |
    38	|--------|------------------|------------------|
    39	| Paper theorem | Matches the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/` | May be linked by source-labelled `\lean{}`; statement-level `\leanok` only when the statement matches |
    40	| Internal proof obligation | Proves a missing intermediate mathematical input from paper hypotheses | May contain a tracked `sorry` while the proof is open |
    41	| Conditional helper | Quarantines an unproved intermediate obligation | Not a paper theorem; no source-labelled `\leanok` |
    42	
    43	It is never allowed to change the public statement of a declaration presented
    44	as the formalization of a source-labelled paper theorem.  At the final assembly
    45	point, the paper theorem must either discharge the extra hypotheses internally,
    46	or remain as the paper-aligned statement with an unfinished proof while the
    47	conditional helper is given a different name.
    48	
    49	The preferred way to expose unfinished work is a named internal theorem or
    50	definition with a precise paper-origin docstring and, if necessary, a tracked
    51	`sorry`.  This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement
    52	of a source-labelled theorem.
    53	
    54	### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily
    55	
    56	| Temporary reason | Explanation |
    57	|------------------|-------------|
    58	| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |
    59	| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |
    60	| **Auditability** | An explicit temporary hypothesis is easier to find than an implicit assumption hidden in prose, provided it is named as proof debt. |
    61	
    62	These reasons do not justify strengthening a paper theorem.  They only explain
    63	why a short-lived helper declaration may exist while its remaining hypotheses
    64	are being actively removed.
    65	
    66	### How to proceed when a proof needs an extra input
    67	
    68	1. **Check the source statement.**  Read the corresponding TeX in
    69	   `references/ldt-paper/` before changing a theorem linked from the blueprint.
    70	2. **Keep the paper-facing declaration source-faithful.**  Boundary hypotheses
    71	   such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances, or
    72	   type-class assumptions may be faithful encodings when they are needed to
    73	   state the mathematics in Lean.  Proof data such as `BridgeInputs`,
    74	   `RepairInput`, `Residual`, `Package`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic
    75	   `Assumptions` is different: it is not a paper assumption unless the cited
    76	   statement says so.
    77	3. **Name the missing intermediate result.**  If the proof uses a mathematical
    78	   fact not yet formalized, state it as a separate proof obligation.  A
    79	   temporary `sorry` in this declaration is preferable to adding the obligation as
    80	   a hypothesis on the paper theorem.
    81	4. **Do not introduce conditional helpers by default.**  A helper whose name
    82	   ends in `_ofObligations` is a quarantine device, not a normal formalization
    83	   pattern.  It may remain temporarily only when it preserves substantial proof
    84	   content that cannot yet be connected to the paper hypotheses, has a tracked
    85	   discharge or deletion target, and has no source-labelled blueprint
    86	   `\leanok`.  If the helper would merely package missing work as an extra
    87	   hypothesis, restore the theorem with the paper statement and leave a tracked
    88	   `sorry` instead.
    89	5. **Audit the final statement.**  Every PR touching a source-labelled theorem
    90	   should compare paper assumptions and Lean assumptions, paper conclusion and
    91	   Lean conclusion, and report whether the Lean statement is exact, has only
    92	   faithful boundary hypotheses, or has extra assumptions.
    93	
    94	If a paper-facing declaration is temporarily proved by calling a conditional
    95	helper whose load-bearing input has not yet been produced from the paper
    96	hypotheses, the proof frontier must be marked explicitly.  The declaration
    97	should carry an `**Unfaithful:**` docstring section naming the non-paper
    98	dependency, citing the paper-gap note or tracking issue, and identifying the
    99	internal theorem that will remove the dependency.  A named proof obligation
   100	with a tracked `sorry` is preferred whenever possible, because it makes the
   101	missing mathematical assertion visible without adding it to the paper theorem
   102	statement.
   103	
   104	### Required metadata for new proof-obligation declarations
   105	
   106	A new declaration whose name contains a proof-debt token such as `Bridge`,
   107	`Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Producer`, `Input`, `Hypotheses`,
   108	`Assumptions`, `Obligation`, or `Witness` must explain its mathematical role in
   109	the def-site docstring.  A paper citation alone is not enough, because the
   110	reviewer must be able to tell whether the declaration is part of the paper
   111	statement or a Lean-only proof obligation.
   112	
   113	Use one of the following markers.
   114	
   115	| Marker | Use |
   116	|--------|-----|
   117	| `**Source:**`, `**Paper source:**`, or `**Source statement:**` | The declaration is a faithful formal encoding of a cited source statement or a field of that statement |
   118	| `**Faithful encoding:**` | The declaration records boundary data or domain data that the paper uses implicitly |
   119	| `**Proof obligation:**` or `**Internal proof obligation:**` | The declaration is a theorem or record that must be proved from the paper hypotheses before a source theorem is complete |
   120	| `**Conditional:**` | The declaration is a conditional helper; it must not be linked as the source theorem |
   121	| `**Unfaithful:**` | The declaration or proof currently depends on a load-bearing assumption not yet derived from the paper hypotheses |
   122	
   123	Proof-obligation, conditional, and unfaithful markers must cite a paper-gap note
   124	or tracking issue and must state the planned discharge or elimination theorem.
   125	If such a declaration would merely package missing work as an added hypothesis
   126	to a source theorem, do not introduce it; restore the source theorem statement
   127	and leave the missing proof as a tracked `sorry`.
   128	
   129	### Conditional helper boundary
   130	
   131	1. **Prefer a source theorem with a tracked `sorry`.**  If a proof requires a
   132	   construction that is not yet available from the paper hypotheses, the first
   133	   repair is to restore the source theorem statement and leave the missing proof
   134	   open.  Do not introduce a new `Input`, `Obligation`, `Residual`, `Repair`,
   135	   `Producer`, or `Package` merely to avoid that `sorry`.
   136	
   137	2. **Do not bundle several missing theorem-level steps into one hypothesis.**
   138	   The former Section 9 bundle `SelfImprovementObligations` and the helper
   139	   `selfImprovementFromObligations` were removed because they bundled
   140	   helper strong self-consistency, orthonormalization, and final-field transport
   141	   into a single route to the full self-improvement conclusion.  The correct
   142	   boundary is now the theorem `selfImprovement`, whose missing
   143	   proof is an explicit `sorry`.
   144	
   145	   The former induction-section helper
   146	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection_ofObligations` was removed because it
   147	   encouraged propagation of the Section 9 bundle into the Section 6 successor
   148	   constructors.  Those constructors now call the theorem
   149	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` directly; its current proof gap is the
   150	   correct place for the missing work.
   151	
   152	3. **Propagation is a warning sign.**  The consumer of
   153	   `selfImprovementInInductionSection` — typically a
   154	   `MainInductionStep` theorem — should close the hypothesis with an internal
   155	   theorem as soon as possible.  If the hypothesis propagates upward toward a
   156	   paper-labelled theorem, the PR should stop and either prove the obligation or
   157	   restore the paper theorem with an explicit unfinished proof.
   158	
   159	4. **Final closure at the paper theorem.**  The theorem `mainFormal` in
   160	   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean` is reserved for the
   161	   paper-shaped statement.  If the witness needed by the final transport has
   162	   not yet been constructed from the paper hypotheses, the theorem should remain
   163	   an explicit unfinished proof.  Do not replace the missing construction by
   164	   extra bridge, residual, repair, package, or obligation hypotheses, and do not
   165	   proliferate named obligation declarations merely to avoid a direct `sorry`.
   166	
   167	   The paper-labelled `mainFormal` should have the hypotheses of the paper
   168	   theorem: a projective strategy passing the low individual degree test, the
   169	   stated parameter bounds, and the faithful formalization of the ambient
   170	   domains.  Bridge, residual, repair, and proof-obligation inputs must be
   171	   produced inside its proof rather than added to its statement.
   172	
   173	### Existing bridge-like declarations
   174	
   175	Several older declarations still name proof obligations explicitly.  They are
   176	transitional proof debt, not a pattern to extend to paper theorem statements.
   177	When such a declaration remains useful, its role should be made explicit and
   178	kept away from source-labelled blueprint entries.
   179	
   180	| Declaration | Status to maintain |
   181	|-------------|--------------------|
   182	| `LdPastingNontrivialContext` | Nontrivial-regime context for `ldPastingNontrivial`; do not present it as the unrestricted `thm:ld-pasting` context |
   183	| `Pasting.ldPastingNontrivial` | Restricted nontrivial-regime form of `thm:ld-pasting`; link from a Lean-only remark, while `Pasting.ldPasting` remains the unrestricted source-facing theorem |
   184	
   185	The former same-carrier `mainFormal` transport-witness route has been retired.
   186	The former `SelfImprovement.HelperStrongSelfConsistencyInput`,
   187	`SelfImprovement.OrthonormalizationInput`, `SelfImprovement.FinalFieldsInput`, and
   188	`MakingMeasurementsProjective.OrthonormalizationInput` bundles have been removed.
   189	Useful proof content should be kept as named construction lemmas, while missing
   190	orthonormalization or final-field arguments remain direct proof gaps on the
   191	source-facing theorem until proved from the paper hypotheses.
   192	
   193	The former `MakingMeasurementsProjective.SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation
   194	has likewise been retired.  The spectral-truncation step is represented by the
   195	source-shaped statement `SpectralTruncationStatement` and by direct construction
   196	theorems such as `spectralTruncationStatement_of_sourceAlmostProjective`,
   197	rather than by an `Input` wrapper passed through later theorems.
   198	
   199	### Retiring auxiliary declarations
   200	
   201	An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
   202	renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all of the following
   203	conditions hold.
   204	
   205	1. It is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
   206	   outside result.
   207	2. No current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated.
   208	3. It assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data, repair
   209	   data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper proof requires.
   210	
   211	If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, keep it
   212	as a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.  It should
   213	not remain a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should not be
   214	the target of a source-labelled blueprint `\leanok`.
   215	
   216	### Former proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean`
   217	
   218	The former direct tracked proof obligations in `MainFormal.lean` and the
   219	Section 6 successor route have been discharged under the corrected source
   220	statements.  The theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` is the corrected
   221	two-space source theorem.  The earlier same-carrier auxiliary interface has
   222	been retired; the headline theorem carries no bridge, residual, repair,
   223	package, producer, generic hypothesis, or proof-obligation input in its public
   224	statement.
   225	
   226	### Distinction from anti-patterns
   227	
   228	This rule addresses the same risk as conclusion-shaped-hypothesis smuggling
   229	(anti-pattern A1 in `docs/anti_patterns.md`), but it is stricter for
   230	paper-labelled declarations:
   231	
   232	- A conclusion-shaped hypothesis is always unacceptable.
   233	- A genuine intermediate fact may appear only in a separately named conditional
   234	  helper while its obligation discharger is being proved.
   235	- That same intermediate fact is still unacceptable as an added hypothesis on
   236	  the public statement of the paper theorem, unless it is a faithful encoding
   237	  of a hypothesis present in the cited source.
   238	
   239	Obligation structures that bundle still-unproved theorem-level steps are proof
   240	debt under this pattern.  They should not be introduced merely because a proof
   241	is blocked.  The preferred repair is to keep the paper-labelled statement
   242	source-faithful and make the exact missing mathematical step visible as a named
   243	lemma or as a `sorry` in the theorem with the paper statement.
   244	
   245	---
   246	
   247	## Pattern 2: Blueprint–Lean synchronization
   248	
   249	### The three tags
   250	
   251	The blueprint (under `blueprint/src/chapter/`) uses three LaTeX commands
   252	to link to Lean:
   253	
   254	| Tag | Meaning | Example |
   255	|-----|---------|---------|
   256	| `\lean{Name}` | The corresponding Lean declaration exists | `\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal}` |
   257	| `\leanok` (statement-level) | The Lean declaration compiles and its statement matches the source or blueprint statement; it does not certify proof closure | `\leanok` |
   258	| `\leanok` (proof-level) | The proof block is fully formalized — the theorem or lemma has a complete sorry-free proof | `\lean{...}` plus `\leanok` inside `\begin{proof}` |
   259	| `\uses{label}` | The statement or proof block depends on the cited result | `\uses{thm:orthonormalization, prop:completing-to-measurement}` |

     5

    39	/-- Retain every good outcome and send every other outcome to the specified
    40	good outcome. The default is actual domain data, with its membership proof. -/
    41	def toGood (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    42	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) (a : α) : {a // good a} :=
    43	  if h : good a then ⟨a, h⟩ else a₀
    44	
    45	omit [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] in
    46	@[simp] theorem toGood_coe (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    47	    (a₀ a : {a // good a}) : toGood good a₀ a = a := by
    48	  simp [toGood, a.property]
    49	
    50	/-- The omitted effects. When the measurement is projective, their sum is the
    51	projection complementary to the sum of good effects. -/
    52	noncomputable def badEffect (M : Measurement α ι)
    53	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] : Op ι :=
    54	  ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => ¬ good a), M.effect a
    55	
    56	/-- Complete the restriction to good outcomes by adding all bad effects to
    57	`a₀`. This is an outcome postprocessing of the original complete measurement. -/
    58	noncomputable def complete (M : Measurement α ι)
    59	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (a₀ : {a // good a}) :
    60	    Measurement {a // good a} ι :=
    61	  M.postprocess (toGood good a₀)
    62	
    63	/-- The completion is projective whenever the original measurement is
    64	projective, by projectivity of outcome postprocessing. -/
    65	theorem complete_isProjective (M : Measurement α ι)
    66	    (hM : Measurement.IsProjective M) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    67	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) : Measurement.IsProjective (complete M good a₀) :=
    68	  SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective M hM (toGood good a₀)
    69	
    70	omit [DecidableEq α] in
    71	/-- The bad effect is precisely the complement of the restricted total. -/
    72	theorem badEffect_eq_one_sub (M : Measurement α ι)
    73	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] :
    74	    badEffect M good = 1 - ∑ a : {a // good a}, M.effect a := by
    75	  have hsplit := Fintype.sum_subtype_add_sum_subtype good M.effect
    76	  have hbad : badEffect M good = ∑ a : {a // ¬ good a}, M.effect a := by
    77	    exact Finset.sum_subtype _ (by simp) M.effect
    78	  rw [hbad]
    79	  rw [M.sum_eq_one] at hsplit
    80	  exact eq_sub_of_add_eq' hsplit
    81	
    82	omit [DecidableEq α] in
    83	/-- The sum of the omitted effects is positive semidefinite. -/
    84	theorem badEffect_nonneg (M : Measurement α ι)
    85	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] : 0 ≤ badEffect M good :=
    86	  Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a

    88	/-- The submeasurement obtained by retaining only the good outcomes. -/
    89	noncomputable def restrict (M : Measurement α ι)
    90	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] : Submeasurement {a // good a} ι where
    91	  effect a := M.effect a
    92	  pos a := M.pos a
    93	  sum_le_one := by
    94	    have h := badEffect_nonneg M good
    95	    rw [badEffect_eq_one_sub] at h
    96	    exact sub_nonneg.mp h

    98	/-- The bad effect is itself a projection: it is one effect of the binary
    99	postprocessing recording whether an outcome is bad. -/
   100	theorem badEffect_isStarProjection (M : Measurement α ι)
   101	    (hM : Measurement.IsProjective M) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] :
   102	    IsStarProjection (badEffect M good) := by
   103	  have h := SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective M hM
   104	    (fun a => decide (¬ good a)) true
   105	  change IsStarProjection (∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter
   106	    (fun a => decide (¬ good a) = true), M.effect a) at h
   107	  simpa only [decide_eq_true_eq, badEffect] using h

   109	/-- The completed default effect absorbs exactly the omitted projection;
   110	all other good effects are retained. -/
   111	theorem complete_effect (M : Measurement α ι)
   112	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (a₀ a : {a // good a}) :
   113	    (complete M good a₀).effect a =
   114	      M.effect a + if a = a₀ then badEffect M good else 0 := by
   115	  classical
   116	  rw [complete, Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter]
   117	  have hterm (b : α) :
   118	      (if toGood good a₀ b = a then M.effect b else 0) =
   119	        (if b = a.val then M.effect b else 0) +
   120	          if a = a₀ then (if ¬ good b then M.effect b else 0) else 0 := by
   121	    by_cases hb : good b
   122	    · have heq : toGood good a₀ b = a ↔ b = a.val := by
   123	        simp [toGood, hb, Subtype.ext_iff]
   124	      simp [heq, hb]
   125	    · have hba : b ≠ a.val := by
   126	        rintro rfl
   127	        exact hb a.property
   128	      simp [toGood, hb, hba, eq_comm]
   129	  simp_rw [hterm]
   130	  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   131	  simp [badEffect, Finset.sum_filter, Finset.sum_ite_irrel]

   133	/-- Relabeling the completed measurement adds the bad effect to exactly the
   134	label of the chosen default outcome, relative to the relabeled restriction. -/
   135	theorem complete_postprocess_effect (M : Measurement α ι)
   136	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (a₀ : {a // good a})
   137	    (g : {a // good a} → β) (b : β) :
   138	    ((complete M good a₀).postprocess g).effect b =
   139	      ((restrict M good).postprocess g).effect b +
   140	        if b = g a₀ then badEffect M good else 0 := by
   141	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   142	  simp_rw [complete_effect]
   143	  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   144	  congr 1
   145	  simp [eq_comm]

   148	    (f : α → β) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :

   158	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

   161	          intro a ha

   219	/-- Equal good-outcome contributions cancel; the remaining averaged change
   220	is bounded by the sum of the bad-outcome upper bounds. -/
   221	private theorem abs_avg_sum_change_le (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
   222	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (u v : X → α → ℝ) (r : α → ℝ)
   223	    (hu : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ u x a ∧ u x a ≤ r a)
   224	    (hv : ∀ x a, 0 ≤ v x a ∧ v x a ≤ r a)
   225	    (huv : ∀ x a, good a → u x a = v x a) (c : ℝ) :
   226	    |avgOver μ (fun x => c - ∑ a, u x a) -
   227	        avgOver μ (fun x => c - ∑ a, v x a)| ≤
   228	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => ¬ good a), r a := by
   229	  have hpoint (x : X) :
   230	      |(c - ∑ a, u x a) - (c - ∑ a, v x a)| ≤
   231	        ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => ¬ good a), r a := by
   232	    have hterm (a : α) : |v x a - u x a| ≤ if ¬ good a then r a else 0 := by
   233	      by_cases ha : good a
   234	      · simp [ha, huv x a ha]
   235	      · rw [if_pos ha]
   236	        exact abs_le.mpr ⟨by linarith [(hu x a).2, (hv x a).1],
   237	          by linarith [(hv x a).2, (hu x a).1]⟩
   238	    calc
   239	      _ = |∑ a, (v x a - u x a)| := by
   240	        rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   241	        congr 1
   242	        ring
   243	      _ ≤ ∑ a, |v x a - u x a| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
   244	      _ ≤ ∑ a, if ¬ good a then r a else 0 :=
   245	        Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => hterm a
   246	      _ = _ := (Finset.sum_filter _ _).symm
   247	  rw [← avgOver_sub]
   248	  calc
   249	    _ ≤ avgOver μ (fun x => |(c - ∑ a, u x a) - (c - ∑ a, v x a)|) := by
   250	      unfold avgOver
   251	      refine (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans_eq ?_
   252	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   253	      intro x _
   254	      rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (μ.nonnegative x)]
   255	    _ ≤ avgOver μ (fun _ =>
   256	        ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => ¬ good a), r a) :=
   257	      avgOver_mono μ _ _ hpoint
   258	    _ = _ := avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ _

   263	This auxiliary isolates the quantitative content of the source completion step. -/
   264	theorem abs_postprocess_consistency_left_sub_le

   266	    (N : X → Measurement β ιB) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]

   287	    (fun x a ha => by rw [hfg x a ha]) _

   289	/-- Relabelings that agree on good outcomes change Bob-first cross-player
   290	consistency by at most Bob's bad-outcome state mass. The completed measurement

   293	theorem abs_postprocess_consistency_right_sub_le
   294	    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (M : Measurement α ιB)
   295	    (N : X → Measurement β ιA) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
   296	    (f g : X → α → β) (hfg : ∀ x a, good a → f x a = g x a)
   297	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :

/-!
# Expanded registers and point measurements

This module adjoins two EPR pairs to a heterogeneous Pauli-basis-test strategy,
records the four register placements used in the analysis, and defines the
expanded point observables and measurements. Fourier inversion identifies their
effects with a convolution of projectors and proves completeness and projectivity.

## References

The constructions formalize blueprint `def:expanded-state`,
`def:expanded-observables`, `def:expanded-point-measurement`, and
`def:expanded-point-trace-projection`. Their paper source is
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-418`.
-/

/-- The six registers `AA'A''BB'B''`, retaining distinct Alice and Bob local
spaces. This is the register index type of `def:expanded-state`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
`def:expanded-state`. -/
abbrev SixReg (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
  (ιA × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    (ιB × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P))

/-- Equality of six-register indices is supplied by classical decidability for
the register type. This is the index set of blueprint
`def:expanded-state`. -/
noncomputable instance sixRegDecidableEq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (ιA ιB : Type*) : DecidableEq (SixReg P ιA ιB) :=
  Classical.decEq _

/-- Reassociate the tensor product of the strategy state and two EPR states
directly into register order `AA'A''BB'B''` for
`eq:def-psihat`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`. -/
def sixRegShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    (((ιA × ιB) × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    (p.1.1.2, (p.2.1, p.2.2)))
  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    (p.2.2.1, p.2.2.2))
  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl

/-- The four placements `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, and `AB''` used explicitly in
the chapter-14 consistency statements. Paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
`def:symmetric-equivalents`. -/
inductive Placement where
  | AA'
  | BA''
  | BB'
  | AB''
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype

/-- The strategy-player side supplying the local Hilbert space in each of the
four register placements at paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`. -/
def Placement.side : Placement → PlayerSide
  | .AA' => .alice
  | .BA'' => .bob
  | .BB' => .bob
  | .AB'' => .alice

+/-! # Encoding-supported Pauli reference measurements
+
+The reference measurement measures the strategy's Pauli answer and an independent
+ideal Pauli answer, then returns the bounded encoding of their sum. Its effects
+vanish outside the encoding image. Evaluation of its polynomial outcome is the
+convolution of the evaluated strategy measurement and the ideal point projectors.
+
+These are internal auxiliary constructions for blueprint `eq:qld-nonencoding-mass`
+and `lem:qld-nonencoding-mass-bound`, not the quantitative support estimate. No
+winning premise or global polynomial-pair witness is used or constructed here.
+
+## References
+
+The encoding is paper `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` in
+`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:882-897`. The convolution is the Pauli
+answer replacement of the expanded point measurement at
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:383-418`.
+The corrected use in `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis` is recorded in blueprint
+`eq:qld-nonencoding-mass` and `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+variable {params : AdmissibleParams} {error : ℝ}
+
+/-- The ideal Pauli basis measurement on the ancillary register, bundled using
+positivity and completeness of the existing Pauli projectors. -/
+noncomputable def pauliRegisterMeas (basis : PauliKind) :
+    Measurement (PauliRegister params) (PauliRegister params) :=
+  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (pauliProj basis)
+    (fun answer => Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr (posSemidef_pauliProj basis answer))
+    (sum_pauliProj_eq_one basis)
+
+/-- Every bounded encoding lies in the full-field decoder's encoding image. -/
+@[simp] theorem isEncoding_encodingPoly (answer : PauliRegister params) :
+    IsEncoding (encodingPoly answer) := by
+  unfold IsEncoding
+  rw [decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding]
+  rfl
+
+namespace ProjectiveSetting
+
+/-- Measure the strategy Pauli answer and the ancillary ideal Pauli answer and
+return the encoding of their sum. This complete POVM is the internal reference
+measurement underlying blueprint `eq:qld-nonencoding-mass`; it is not the global
+polynomial measurement whose existence is required in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
+noncomputable def encodingPauliMeas (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) :
+    Measurement (Poly params) (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
+  (tensorMeasurement (setting.pauliMeas side basis) (pauliRegisterMeas basis)).postprocess
+    fun answers => encodingPoly (answers.1 + answers.2)
+
+/-- The reference effect sums the product effects over pairs whose sum encodes
+the specified polynomial representative. -/
+theorem encodingPauliMeas_effect (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) (poly : Poly params) :
+    (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).effect poly =
+      ∑ answers ∈ Finset.univ.filter
+          (fun answers : PauliRegister params × PauliRegister params =>
+            encodingPoly (answers.1 + answers.2) = poly),
+        heteroKron ((setting.pauliMeas side basis).effect answers.1)
+          (pauliProj basis answers.2) :=
+  rfl
+
+/-- Positivity is preserved by the tensor product and the encoding postprocessing. -/
+theorem encodingPauliMeas_effect_nonneg (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) (poly : Poly params) :
+    0 ≤ (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).effect poly :=
+  (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).pos poly
+
+/-- The reference effects sum to the identity on the strategy and ancillary registers. -/
+theorem sum_encodingPauliMeas_effect_eq_one (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) :
+    ∑ poly, (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).effect poly = 1 :=
+  (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).sum_eq_one
+
+/-- A nonencoding polynomial has zero reference effect. This is exact support of
+the auxiliary measurement, not a bound on the global polynomial measurement. -/
+theorem encodingPauliMeas_effect_eq_zero_of_not_isEncoding
+    (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error) (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind)
+    (poly : Poly params) (hpoly : ¬ IsEncoding poly) :
+    (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).effect poly = 0 := by
+  classical
+  rw [encodingPauliMeas_effect]
+  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+  intro answers hanswers
+  exact False.elim (hpoly ((Finset.mem_filter.mp hanswers).2 ▸
+    isEncoding_encodingPoly (answers.1 + answers.2)))
+
+/-- Evaluating the reference polynomial is equivalent to evaluating the two Pauli
+answers separately and adding their values. This uses linearity of the encoding,
+not the decoder/evaluation identity for arbitrary polynomial representatives. -/
+theorem encodingPauliMeas_postprocess_eval (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind) (point : Fin params.m → PauliScalar params) :
+    (setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).postprocess (fun poly => evalPoly poly point) =
+      (tensorMeasurement (setting.pauliEvalMeas side basis point)
+        ((pauliRegisterMeas basis).postprocess
+          (fun answer => lowDegreeEnc answer point))).postprocess
+        (fun values => values.1 + values.2) := by
+  unfold encodingPauliMeas pauliEvalMeas
+  rw [Measurement.postprocess_comp, tensorMeasurement_postprocess,
+    Measurement.postprocess_comp]
+  apply congrArg ((tensorMeasurement (setting.pauliMeas side basis)
+    (pauliRegisterMeas basis)).postprocess)
+  funext answers
+  change lowDegreeEnc (answers.1 + answers.2) point =
+    lowDegreeEnc answers.1 point + lowDegreeEnc answers.2 point
+  simp only [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct, add_dotProduct]
+
+/-- The evaluated reference effects are exactly the Pauli-answer convolution
+`K^u_a` in the proof of blueprint `eq:qld-nonencoding-mass`. This identity makes no
+approximation or assertion of consistency with the strategy's point measurement. -/
+theorem encodingPauliMeas_eval_effect_eq_convolution
+    (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error) (side : PlayerSide) (basis : PauliKind)
+    (point : Fin params.m → PauliScalar params) (value : PauliScalar params) :
+    ((setting.encodingPauliMeas side basis).postprocess
+      (fun poly => evalPoly poly point)).effect value =
+      ∑ values ∈ Finset.univ.filter
+          (fun values : PauliScalar params × PauliScalar params => values.1 + values.2 = value),
+        heteroKron ((setting.pauliEvalMeas side basis point).effect values.1)
+          (tauPointProj basis point values.2) := by
+  rw [encodingPauliMeas_postprocess_eval, Measurement.postprocess_effect]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro values _
+  change heteroKron ((setting.pauliEvalMeas side basis point).effect values.1)
+    (((pauliRegisterMeas basis).postprocess
+      (fun answer => lowDegreeEnc answer point)).effect values.2) = _
+  simp only [Measurement.postprocess_effect, lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
+  rfl
+
+end ProjectiveSetting
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    36	/-- Successful completed evaluation means evaluation at every parameter
    37	presenting the point, including when the line direction is zero. -/
    38	theorem directEvalOpt_eq_some_iff {params : DirectLdParams} {degree : ℕ}
    39	    (line : DirectLineDesc params) (point : Fin params.m → DirectScalarQ params)
    40	    (coeffs : DirectDegPoly params degree) (answer : DirectScalarQ params) :
    41	    directEvalOpt line point coeffs = some answer ↔
    42	      DirectEvaluatesTo line coeffs point answer := by
    43	  classical
    44	  unfold directEvalOpt
    45	  split_ifs with hexists
    46	  · simp only [Option.some.injEq]
    47	    constructor
    48	    · intro heq
    49	      simpa [heq] using Classical.choose_spec hexists
    50	    · intro heval
    51	      obtain ⟨parameter, hparameter⟩ := heval.1
    52	      exact ((Classical.choose_spec hexists).2 parameter hparameter).symm.trans
    53	        (heval.2 parameter hparameter)
    54	  · simp only [false_iff]
    55	    exact fun heval => hexists ⟨answer, heval⟩
    56	
    57	/-- The axis answer length fits inside the extended-line coefficient list. -/
    58	theorem axis_degree_le (params : AdmissibleParams) :
    59	    params.d + 1 ≤ params.m * params.d + 2 := by
    60	  have hmul := Nat.mul_le_mul_right params.d params.one_le_m
    61	  omega
    62	
    63	/-- Restrict an extended-line answer to the axis degree bound. -/
    64	def axisRead (params : AdmissibleParams)
    65	    (coeffs : DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1)) :
    66	    DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd params.d :=
    67	  fun index => coeffs (Fin.castLE (axis_degree_le params) index)
    68	
    69	/-- Restriction preserves evaluation when the discarded coefficients vanish. -/
    70	theorem axisRead_eval (params : AdmissibleParams)
    71	    (coeffs : DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1))
    72	    (hsupport : ∀ index, params.d < index.val → coeffs index = 0)
    73	    (parameter : DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd) :
    74	      evalCoefficient (axisRead params coeffs) parameter = evalCoefficient coeffs parameter := by
    75	  unfold evalCoefficient axisRead
    76	  refine Fintype.sum_of_injective (Fin.castLE (axis_degree_le params))
    77	    (Fin.castLE_injective _) _ (fun index => coeffs index * parameter ^ index.val)
    78	    ?_ (fun _ => rfl)
    79	  intro index hindex
    80	  have hlarge : params.d < index.val := by
    81	    by_contra hlarge
    82	    exact hindex ⟨⟨index.val, by omega⟩, Fin.ext rfl⟩
    83	  simp [hsupport index hlarge]
    84	
    85	/-- The extended-line degree fits the direct game's diagonal answer bound. -/
    86	theorem diagonal_degree_le (params : AdmissibleParams) :
    87	    params.m * params.d + 2 ≤
    88	      params.extendedDirectLd.m * params.extendedDirectLd.d + 1 := by
    89	  change params.m * params.d + 2 ≤ (2 * params.m + 2) * params.d + 1
    90	  have hdegree := params.hd
    91	  nlinarith
    92	
    93	/-- Extend a diagonal-line coefficient list by zeros, without changing its polynomial. -/
    94	def diagonalRead (params : AdmissibleParams)
    95	    (coeffs : DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1)) :
    96	    DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd
    97	      (params.extendedDirectLd.m * params.extendedDirectLd.d) :=
    98	  fun index => if bound : index.val < params.m * params.d + 2
    99	    then coeffs ⟨index.val, bound⟩ else 0
   100	
   101	/-- Extending a diagonal answer by zeros preserves evaluation at every parameter. -/
   102	theorem diagonalRead_eval (params : AdmissibleParams)
   103	    (coeffs : DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1))
   104	    (parameter : DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd) :
   105	    evalCoefficient (diagonalRead params coeffs) parameter =
   106	      evalCoefficient coeffs parameter := by
   107	  symm
   108	  apply Fintype.sum_of_injective (Fin.castLE (diagonal_degree_le params))
   109	    (Fin.castLE_injective _) _ _ ?_ ?_
   110	  · intro index hindex
   111	    have hlarge : ¬index.val < params.m * params.d + 2 := by
   112	      intro hsmall
   113	      exact hindex ⟨⟨index.val, hsmall⟩, Fin.ext rfl⟩
   114	    simp [diagonalRead, hlarge]
   115	  · intro index
   116	    simp [diagonalRead, index.isLt]

   136	theorem axis_description_canonical (params : DirectLdParams) (sample : DirectLdSpace params) :

   142	also for zero directions. -/
   143	theorem diagonal_description_canonical (params : DirectLdParams)
   144	    (sample : DirectLdSpace params) :
   145	    directDLineDescOf params (directLdMap params .dline sample) =

   154	/-- On degree-supported outcomes, the axis verifier checks precisely successful
   155	completed evaluation, after the canonical field transport. -/
   156	theorem axisAnswer_win_iff (params : AdmissibleParams)
   157	    (sample : DirectLdSpace params.extendedDirectLd)
   158	    (coeffs : DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1))
   159	    (hsupport : ∀ index, params.d < index.val → coeffs index = 0)
   160	    (answer : DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd) :
   161	    directLdWinPredicate params.extendedDirectLd
   162	      (.aline, directLdMap params.extendedDirectLd .aline sample)
   163	      (.point, directLdMap params.extendedDirectLd .point sample)
   164	      (axisAnswer params coeffs) (pointAnswer params ((extendedDirectScalarEquiv params) answer)) =
   165	        true ↔ directEvalOpt (directALineDescOf params.extendedDirectLd sample)
   166	          sample.point coeffs = some answer := by
   167	  rw [directEvalOpt_eq_some_iff]
   168	  simp only [directLdWinPredicate, axisAnswer, pointAnswer, validDirectLdAnswer,
   169	    Bool.and_self, ↓reduceIte, decide_eq_true_eq,
   170	    RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply, directAlinePointCondition]
   171	  change (∀ parameter, sample.point = _ + parameter • _ →
   172	    ∀ _ : Fin 1, evalCoefficient (axisRead params coeffs) parameter = answer) ↔
   173	    (∃ parameter, sample.point = _ + parameter • _) ∧
   174	      ∀ parameter, sample.point = _ + parameter • _ → evalCoefficient coeffs parameter = answer

   176	  exact (and_iff_right (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap

   181	theorem diagonalAnswer_win_iff (params : AdmissibleParams)
   182	    (sample : DirectLdSpace params.extendedDirectLd)
   183	    (coeffs : DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1))
   184	    (answer : DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd) :

   186	      (.dline, directLdMap params.extendedDirectLd .dline sample)

   208	/-- The actual answer measurement at each direct-game question. No strategy
   209	passing premise or producer of the supplied line witness is used. -/
   210	def answerMeasurement (lines : ExtendedLinesWitness setting points deltaL)
   211	    (side : PlayerSide) (question : DirectLdQuestion params.extendedDirectLd) :
   212	    Measurement (DirectLdAnswer params.extendedDirectLd) (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   213	  match question.1 with
   214	  | .point =>
   215	    let point := directPointToPauli params question.2.point
   216	    (points.extendedQ side (projX point) (projZ point)
   217	      (point (alphaVar params.m)) (point (betaVar params.m))).postprocess (pointAnswer params)
   218	  | .aline =>
   219	    (lines.Qline side (directALineDescOf params.extendedDirectLd question.2)).postprocess
   220	      (axisAnswer params)
   221	  | .dline =>
   222	    (lines.Qline side (directDLineDescOf params.extendedDirectLd question.2)).postprocess
   223	      (diagonalAnswer params)

   225	/-- All wrong-tag effects vanish: the measurement construction never uses the
   226	game's wrong-format fallback answers. -/
   227	theorem answerMeasurement_effect_eq_zero
   228	    (lines : ExtendedLinesWitness setting points deltaL) (side : PlayerSide)
   229	    (question : DirectLdQuestion params.extendedDirectLd)
   230	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer params.extendedDirectLd)
   231	    (hanswer : validDirectLdAnswer question.1 answer = false) :
   232	    (answerMeasurement lines side question).effect answer = 0 := by
   233	  classical
   234	  rcases question with ⟨kind, question⟩
   235	  cases kind <;> cases answer <;>
   236	    simp_all [validDirectLdAnswer, answerMeasurement,
   237	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement.postprocess,
   238	      pointAnswer, axisAnswer, diagonalAnswer]
   239	
   240	/-- The point measurements are projective by coarse-graining the supplied joint
   241	projective measurements. This does not invoke the unfinished `extendedQ_spec`. -/
   242	theorem point_answerMeasurement_isProjective
   243	    (lines : ExtendedLinesWitness setting points deltaL) (side : PlayerSide)
   244	    (question : DirectLdSpace params.extendedDirectLd) :
   245	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (answerMeasurement lines side (.point, question)) := by
   246	  apply SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective
   247	  apply SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective
   248	  exact points.projective _ _ _

   250	/-- Axis truncation preserves evaluation on every nonzero effect, directly by
   251	the degree-support field of the supplied extended-line witness. -/
   252	theorem axisRead_eval_of_effect_ne_zero
   253	    (lines : ExtendedLinesWitness setting points deltaL) (side : PlayerSide)
   254	    (line : DirectLineDesc params.extendedDirectLd) (hline : line.kind = .axis)
   255	    (coeffs : DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1))

    39	/-- Identify the direct extended game's scalar field with the Pauli scalar
    40	field.  Both are selected by `fixedFieldModel`; only their proof argument for
    41	admissibility differs. -/
    42	noncomputable def extendedDirectScalarEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    43	    DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd ≃+* PauliScalar P := by
    44	  have h : P.extendedDirectLd.hq = P.hq := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    45	  cases h
    46	  exact RingEquiv.refl _
    47	
    48	/-- Transport an extended direct point into the canonical Pauli scalar field. -/
    49	def directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
    50	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m -> DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    51	    Fin (2 * P.m + 2) -> PauliScalar P :=
    52	  fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (u i)

    54	/-! ## Combined point and line measurements -/
    55	
    56	/-- Projective joint point measurements and their ordered consistency
    57	guarantees from `lem:qld-4-10`, paper lines 689--709.  The `XZ` and `ZX`
    58	products are retained as distinct fields. -/
    59	structure CombinedPointsWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    60	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (δ : ℝ) where
    61	  /-- The complete joint measurement on each player's expanded local space. -/
    62	  Q : (side : PlayerSide) ->
    63	    (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) ->
    64	    (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) ->
    65	    Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
    66	  /-- Every joint point measurement is projective. -/
    67	  projective : ∀ side x z, Measurement.IsProjective (Q side x z)
    68	  /-- Joint point measurements agree across every directed opposite placement. -/
    69	  self_consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    70	    opFamilyDistSq
    71	      (uniformDistribution
    72	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
    73	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    74	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2 ((Q p2.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    75	      S.psiHat <= δ
    76	  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `X`-then-`Z` product. -/
    77	  consistent_XZ : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    78	    opFamilyDistSq
    79	      (uniformDistribution
    80	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
    81	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    82	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2
    83	        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
    84	          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
    85	      S.psiHat <= δ
    86	  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product. -/
    87	  consistent_ZX : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    88	    opFamilyDistSq
    89	      (uniformDistribution
    90	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
    91	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
    92	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2
    93	        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
    94	          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
    95	      S.psiHat <= δ
    96	
    97	/-- Joint line measurements and their evaluation consistency from
    98	`lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper lines 882--894.  Evaluation uses explicit `Option`
    99	outcomes, including the class of answers not determined at the sampled point. -/
   100	structure CombinedLinesWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
   101	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
   102	    (δ : ℝ) where
   103	  /-- The complete paired-line measurement on each expanded local space. -/
   104	  T : (side : PlayerSide) ->
   105	    LineDesc P.toLdParams -> LineDesc P.toLdParams ->
   106	    Measurement
   107	      (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   108	        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
   109	      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   110	  /-- On an axis-parallel X line, outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
   111	  axis_degree_X : ∀ side lineX lineZ fX fZ,
   112	    lineX.kind = .axis -> Not (DegPoly.FitsDegree P.d fX) ->
   113	      (T side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0
   114	  /-- On an axis-parallel Z line, outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
   115	  axis_degree_Z : ∀ side lineX lineZ fX fZ,
   116	    lineZ.kind = .axis -> Not (DegPoly.FitsDegree P.d fZ) ->
   117	      (T side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0
   118	  /-- Evaluated line pairs are consistent with the completed point-pair
   119	  measurement on every directed opposite placement. -/
   120	  consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   121	    consistencyDefect
   122	      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist P.toLdParams)

    66	
    67	Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple of the Pauli basis
    68	test, $\ket{\hat\psi}$ is the expanded state of the projective strategy
    69	under analysis, succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all
    70	approximations are with respect to $\ket{\hat\psi}$.  For lines
    71	$\ell_X, \ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$, the POVM $\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$,
    72	with outcomes pairs of polynomials of degree at most $md$ on the two
    73	lines, is the two-basis combined line measurement, and
    74	$\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is the combined point measurement; their
    75	consistency errors are $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$ and
    76	$\delta_Q = \poly(\eps)$ respectively, and

    79	measurement $\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, built for each line $\ell$ in
    80	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, is $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$-consistent, on average over
    81	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$, with the combined point
    82	measurement on the extended coordinates, together with the
    83	register-swapped counterpart.%

   122	The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
   123	input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
   124	point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
   125	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   126	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   127	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   128	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   129	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.

   132	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   133	order

   136	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   137	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q

   299	\section{The source assertion and the two routes}
   300	
   301	The source proof in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} constructs $\hat Q^{\ell}_f$ by
   302	averaging, over a distribution $D$ on tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$
   303	provided by its sub-line lemma, the pushforward of
   304	$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ along a combining map, and reduces the lemma to a
   305	bound on the scalar consistency defect
   306	\begin{equation}
   307	  \Lambda \,=\,
   308	  \E_{(\ell,\ell_X,\ell_Z) \sim D}\
   309	  \E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta) \in \ell}
   310	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   311	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   312	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   313	  \ket{\hat\psi}\,,
   314	  \tag{\path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}}
   315	\end{equation}
   316	in which the point $(x,z,\alpha,\beta)$ is uniform on $\ell$ and the sum
   317	ranges over pairs of line polynomials.  The proof then bounds $\Lambda$
   318	twice, by different routes and with different results, and the printed
   319	record is internally inconsistent: the display introducing $\Lambda$
   320	asserts the first-route bound, while the closing lines assert the
   321	second-route bound as the operative one; the lemma statement claims a
   322	third form matching neither.
   323	
   324	\paragraph{The first route.}
   325	Three claims are chained.  The combined point measurement
   326	$\hat Q^{x,z}$ is replaced by the ordered product of the two point
   327	measurements at cost $\delta_Q^{1/2}$; the $X$-point factor is removed at
   328	cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$; and the remaining $Z$-point
   329	correlation is shown to be within
   330	$\sqrt{m}\,(\delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} + \eps^{1/4})$ of one.  The
   331	factors of $m$ enter through the mixture structure of the sub-line
   332	distribution: each restricted line distribution carries mixture weight
   333	$1/(2m)$ in the line-point distribution, so an average bounded by
   334	$\delta$ over the full distribution is bounded only by $2m\delta$ over a
   335	restricted component and by $4m^2\delta$ over a product of two
   336	components, and the Cauchy--Schwarz steps halve the exponents.  Chaining
   337	the claims gives
   338	\begin{equation*}
   339	  \Lambda \,=\, O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   340	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)
   341	  \,=\, m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)\,.
   342	\end{equation*}
   343	One intermediate assertion needs a harmless correction: the final line
   344	of the proof of the second claim asserts the bound
   345	$O(m^2 \delta_{\mathrm{Line}})$ for a consistency term that is close to
   346	one, rather than for its deficit.  Read as a bound on the deficit ---
   347	which is what the surrounding Cauchy--Schwarz argument requires and what
   348	the invoked line--point consistency provides after the mixture
   349	inflation --- the claim and its use are correct, with the square root of
   350	the deficit giving the stated cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$.
   351	
   352	\paragraph{The second route.}
   353	After the chain, the source restarts: it asserts that, by Property~2 of
   354	its sub-line lemma, $\Lambda$ is a mixture, over types
   355	$\mathrm{v}_1, \mathrm{v}_2 \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and
   356	indices $i, j \in \{1, \dots, m\}$, of terms
   357	\begin{equation*}
   358	  \E_{(\ell_X, x) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_1,i}}\
   359	  \E_{(\ell_Z, z) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_2,j}}
   360	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   361	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   362	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   363	  \ket{\hat\psi}
   364	\end{equation*}
   365	over two \emph{independently} sampled restricted line-point pairs,
   366	bounds each term by $O(m^2\delta_P)$ using the restricted-distribution
   367	consequence of the two-basis line lemma, and concludes
   368	$\Lambda = O(m^2\delta_P)$.  The invoked decomposition concerns the
   369	\emph{joint} law of the pair $((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z))$, where $x$ and
   370	$z$ are the two blocks of the single point sampled on $\ell$.  Property~2
   371	of the sub-line lemma does not assert this joint law: it asserts the
   372	component-wise product law of the pair of \emph{lines}
   373	$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, and the conditional uniformity of each point on its
   374	line separately --- equivalently, the laws of the two pairs
   375	$((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z'))$ and $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, z))$ in which
   376	the \emph{other} point is resampled independently.  These marginal
   377	statements are exactly what the first route's claims consume, each
   378	involving one point at a time; the joint decomposition used by the
   379	second route is a strictly stronger property and is not established by
   380	the lemma it is attributed to.

   389	Hence the established derivation supports no bound of the claimed form.
